title: Unpacking METR’s findings: Does AI slow developers down?
summary: A METR study participant explains why developers overestimate AI speedup, and gives practical advice on context rot, time-boxing, idle time and mapping tasks to model strengths.

assertions.quote: I think everyone um estimates speed up because it's just it's so much fun to use AI.
it was en more enjoyable to talk back and forth to an AI than it was to grind myself on a bug

verdicts.note: Developers said ChatGPT eased their cognitive load, yet in the follow-up experiment the ChatGPT group spent more total time (less on coding tasks, more on multiple-choice). Perceived effort fell while elapsed time did not.

assertions.quote: documentation, unit tests, refactoring, these things, AI oneshots
GPU kernels like those are kind of out of distribution for models right now.

verdicts.note: Kernel and parallelism code remained a weak spot through 2025, though specialized models and agents improved on kernel benchmarks by 2026.

assertions.quote: People need to sort of fast fail. So like sort of time box when you're working with an L.

verdicts.note: Workflow advice that is plausible but has not been directly measured.

METR: developers accepted <44% of generations, and one 'wasted at least an hour' trying with AI before reverting and doing the work by hand. That documents the sunk-cost loss, but the time-boxing remedy was not tested.

assertions.quote: you end up with this huge bloated codebase because an LLM is trying to work with kernels

verdicts.note: Self-rated code complexity did not differ with workplace AI use (Table 11), but the follow-up found lower maintainability and more technical debt. The burden part is supported, the complexity part is not.

assertions.quote: what good code looks like makes it easier for me to realize when a model is producing, you know, bad code, bloated code
models start to get overwhelmed with irrelevant information and they start getting confused.
you feed the chat into a model to summarize it down.
that will be much more effective than continuing to fight within the same chat.
reasoning models have made this so much worse because the response time is now solidly out of the human attention span.
